accepted.title: Geometric three-manifold characterization of nonhyperbolic separable free-by-cyclic groups
accepted.text: A free-by-cyclic group here means G=F_r⋊_ΦZ with F_r nontrivial and of finite rank. If G is not word-hyperbolic and is subgroup separable, must G be commensurable with the fundamental group of a geometric3-manifold? Subgroup separable means every finitely generated subgroup is closed in the profinite topology; commensurable means the two groups have isomorphic finite-index subgroups. Geometric refers to a manifold carrying one of Thurston’s eight geometries; no closedness assumption is added.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

accepted.title: Quasiconvexity or virtual fibre for hyperbolic free-by-cyclic subgroups
accepted.text: A free-by-cyclic group here means G=F_r⋊_ΦZ with F_r nontrivial and of finite rank. If G is word-hyperbolic, is every finitely generated H≤G quasiconvex unless H is a virtual fibre or virtual semi-fibre of some free-by-cyclic subgroup G₀≤G containing H? A virtual fibre means that after passing to a finite-index G₁≤G₀, H∩G₁ is the kernel of a homomorphism G₁→Z; a virtual semi-fibre means that some such G₁ is a proper ascending HNN extension with base H∩G₁. Quasiconvex means geodesics between elements of H in a Cayley graph of G stay a uniformly bounded distance from H.

accepted.title: Subgroup separability versus virtual BNS symmetry
accepted.text: A free-by-cyclic group here means G=F_r⋊_ΦZ with F_r nontrivial and of finite rank. Write Σ¹(K) for the Bieri–Neumann–Strebel invariant: nonzero real character rays whose nonnegative-level subgraph of a Cayley graph is connected; symmetry means [χ]∈Σ¹(K) iff [−χ]∈Σ¹(K). For G word-hyperbolic with irreducible monodromy Φ, is G subgroup separable if and only if Σ¹(G₁) is symmetric for every finite-index subgroup G₁≤G? Irreducible means Φ preserves no nontrivial proper free-factor system of F_r.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

accepted.title: Existence of regular profinite identifications for free-by-cyclic groups
accepted.text: A free-by-cyclic group here means G=F_r⋊_ΦZ with F_r nontrivial and of finite rank. Here K^fab is K^ab modulo its torsion subgroup.

accepted.title: Twisted Alexander polynomials detect semifibering in free-by-cyclic groups
accepted.text: A free-by-cyclic group here means G=F_r⋊_ΦZ with F_r nontrivial and of finite rank. Write Σ¹(K) for the Bieri–Neumann–Strebel invariant: nonzero real character rays whose nonnegative-level subgraph of a Cayley graph is connected; symmetry means [χ]∈Σ¹(K) iff [−χ]∈Σ¹(K). For each field F∈{Q,F_p:p prime}, does every such G have the following property for every nonzero χ:G→Z? Either [χ] or [−χ] lies in Σ¹(G) if and only if, for every epimorphism α:G→Q_f to a finite group, the modules H_i(G;F[Q_f][t,t⁻¹]) have rank0 over F[t,t⁻¹] for i=0,1. The coefficient action is g·(a⊗t^j)=α(g)a⊗t^{j+χ(g)}. Equivalently, all these twisted Alexander polynomials are nonzero; this property is G∈TAP₁(F).
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
